t: This is Hans Crescent, a curved street in the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea. It's named after Hans Sloane, the Anglo-Irish physician, naturalist and collector. Sloane left his collection of around seventy-one thousand items to the British nation when he died, and that gift provided the foundation for the British Museum, the British Library and the Natural History Museum. So the name here points back to one of the most generous bequests in London's history, and to a man whose curiosity shaped the city's museums.
